vrio.title: VRIO scorecard
vrio.description: The capabilities the organization actually uses, classified with the VRIO frame across {{headcount}} people. Value = {{value}}% economic weight + {{crit}}% criticality; a dimension counts as present from the {{threshold}}th percentile of our own capabilities.
vrio.descriptionIdle: The capabilities the organization actually uses, classified with the VRIO frame.
vrio.errorMessage: Could not load the VRIO scorecard
vrio.emptyDescription: No skill group is required by a position or held by a person in this tenant.
vrio.caption: VRIO scorecard by capability
vrio.method: The four columns are percentiles across this tenant's own capability set, with the raw measure beneath. Percentiles are used because the raw scales are not calibrated: on live data rarity, inimitability and organization nearly all sit above 0.50, so an absolute cut would mark them present everywhere and collapse the verdict onto Value alone. The verdict is Barney's classification, never an average of the four dimensions.

orgHealth.title: Organizational health
orgHealth.description: Health index per org-unit, computed from engagement, goals, flight risk, attendance, reviews and capability maturity.
orgHealth.errorMessage: Could not load the health index
orgHealth.emptyDescription: No org-unit has people assigned in this tenant.
orgHealth.caption: Health index by org-unit
orgHealth.noData: No data for this dimension: it leaves the calculation instead of counting as zero.
orgHealth.method: The index runs from {{min}} to {{max}} (median {{median}}, spread {{spread}} points). Two readings side by side: STATUS says whether the unit is healthy in absolute terms, STANDING says where to look first relative to the others. Both are needed — with a narrow range, status alone would report "no problem anywhere", while standing alone would brand a merely last-placed unit as failing. A dimension without data leaves the calculation and lowers coverage, not the score.
orgHealth.methodIdle: Status says whether the unit is healthy in absolute terms, standing says where to look first relative to the others. A dimension without data leaves the calculation and lowers coverage, not the score.

advisor.description: Recommendations derived from the capability, VRIO and organizational-health scorecards. Every piece of advice starts from real data and carries its source: nothing here is generated by a language model.
advisor.caption: Recommendations by priority, each with the sources it derives from.
advisor.emptyDescription: On the current data no rule found a situation to act on. This is not an error: it is the absence of cases.
advisor.errorMessage: The recommendations could not be computed.

rule.capabilityGapAcquire: “{{capability}}” is required by {{positions}} positions ({{critical}} critical) and nobody holds it: acquire it through hiring or training.
rule.unusedAdvantageDeploy: “{{capability}}” is an advantage the organization is not exploiting: {{holders}} people hold it, yet only {{covered}} of {{required}} requirements are covered. This is an assignment problem, not a hiring one.
rule.essentialMasteryFragile: “{{capability}}” is essential but mastery is fragile: {{holders}} holders, average level {{heldRank}} of 6, verified on {{verifiedShare}}%. It needs consolidating and testing.
rule.laggingUnitIntervene: “{{unit}}” is among the lagging units (index {{index}}): the dimension holding it back is {{dimension}}, at {{dimensionScore}} of 100.
rule.insufficientCoverageInstrument: For “{{unit}}” the model only has {{coverage}}% of the data ({{missing}} missing): the index is not a diagnosis, it is a missing measurement.
